data.title: Result
data.tagline: Explain the final outcome and the next available step
data.description: A result page or panel marks the end of a task, such as payment success, submission failure, or an empty permission state. State what happened, what it means, and what the user can do next. Do not leave them at a decorative success or error icon.

use: A process failed with a recovery path
avoid: Use a full result page for a tiny local action
Show success before the server confirms it
Report failure without a retry or support path
Use a vague title that does not say what finished

lessonPractice.title: A payment request has finished and produced an order. The user needs the outcome, order number, and available next step. How should the page respond?

options.label: Show a clear result page with status, order information, and the most relevant next action
options.feedback: Payment ends a complete flow, so one result state lets users verify completion and find the next path.

options.label: Show Operation successful for two seconds and automatically return to the store home
options.feedback: Brief feedback provides no order evidence or follow-up and may disappear before users know which payment it refers to.

options.label: Clear the cart and show No products, leaving users to infer that payment succeeded
options.feedback: An empty cart only describes current contents. It does not prove payment outcome or explain failure and processing states.

data.agentPrompt: Create a payment result state that explicitly shows success, failure, or processing, includes order number and amount, and emphasizes only the most relevant next action. Do not imply success from an empty cart; test all three outcomes.
